title: From national direction to action

blocks.heading: From national direction to action
blocks.text: National Development Plans provide direction by connecting development priorities to actions and intended results. Planning identifies the problem, the objective and the resources available. Implementation puts decisions into practice through assigned responsibilities and a timetable. Monitoring checks what was delivered and whether it helped produce the intended outcome. Evaluation uses that evidence to judge progress and decide what to change. A plan can coordinate activities, but its existence does not guarantee that resources arrive or actions are carried out.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: A worked planning sequence
blocks.text: In a fictional district, long journeys prevent access to skills training. The objective is to improve usable access. Planners first identify affected communities and the size of the access problem. They then choose a feasible response, allocate funds and assign responsibility for transport or local provision. During implementation they record what is delivered and who can use it. Monitoring compares attendance and completion with the starting position and the aim. If attendance remains low, the district investigates the remaining barrier and changes the action rather than simply declaring the project complete.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Output and outcome
blocks.text: Vehicles purchased or lessons scheduled are outputs. Improved access and completion are outcomes. A vehicle without a driver or reliable maintenance may not improve access. In a fictional programme, two vehicles are purchased as planned, but use reaches only 30% of intended learners because one route cannot operate. The purchase target is met while the access outcome remains limited. Judge the evidence at the level of the stated objective.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Keep the development purpose in view
blocks.text: Topic 1.1 explains why income, services and participation are different dimensions. Topic 10.1 explains evidence collection. A useful planning account connects resources, responsible action and measurable outcomes instead of listing ambitions without implementation.
